content.title: About
content.content: Pickled eggs are hard‑boiled chicken eggs that have been peeled and soaked in a brine made with vinegar, spices, and sometimes vegetables. They have a firm texture, a mildly sour taste, and a distinctive spice aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickled eggs are a traditional snack in Eastern Europe and Russia, especially during holidays.
Typical brine ingredients include vinegar, salt, sugar, mustard, pepper, bay leaf, and coriander.
When fully submerged in brine, they can be kept in the refrigerator for 2–3 weeks.
In some regions beetroot is added to the brine, giving the eggs a bright red color.
Pickled eggs are often served as a bar snack with beer or as part of salads.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide complete protein that supports muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D helps maintain bone health and supports immune function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Eggs supply selenium, phosphorus, and iron, important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: Fermentation in the brine can promote beneficial bacteria, aiding gut microbiota balance.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins, ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled eggs are salty; people with hypertension should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: If the brine is not acidic enough or eggs are stored at improper temperatures, harmful bacteria can grow.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; those with elevated cholesterol levels should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled eggs can be eaten straight as a snack, sliced into salads, added to sandwiches, or used as a garnish for canapés. They are usually served cold, sometimes with mustard or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled eggs in the refrigerator in a sealed container, fully covered by brine. At 0‑4 °C they stay good for 2–3 weeks. Discard any eggs if the brine becomes cloudy, develops an off‑odor, or changes color.
